# Automatic task sheets {#sec-fichas-auto}

```{r}
#| include: false
source(file.path(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), "..", "..", "R", "libro.R"))
source(file.path(dirname(knitr::current_input(dir = TRUE)), "..", "..", "R", "ficha_auto.R"))
rl <- raiz_libro()
C <- utils::read.csv(file.path(rl, "datos", "agregados", "CATALOGO", "Catalogo.csv"), encoding = "UTF-8", check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
A <- C[file.exists(file.path(rl, "fichas", "auto", paste0(C$tarea_canonica, ".en.qmd"))), ]
lee <- function(t, h) { f <- file.path(rl, "datos", "agregados", paste0("AUTO_", t), paste0(h, ".csv")); if (file.exists(f)) leer(paste0("AUTO_", t), h) else data.frame() }
mx <- function(v) if (length(v) && any(is.finite(v))) max(v, na.rm = TRUE) else NA
DOM <- c(HFON = "Phonological skills", LECTURA = "Reading", L_ORAL = "Oral language", ESCRITURA = "Spelling and writing", MATE = "Numerical cognition",
         HVIS = "Visual-attentional skills", F_EJEC = "Executive functions")
FAM <- c(A = "Accuracy", B = "Rapid naming", C = "Oral reading fluency", D = "Time-limited efficiency", E = "Decision with response time", F = "Span and memory", G = "Comprehension")
R <- do.call(rbind, lapply(A$tarea_canonica, function(t) {
  ct <- A[A$tarea_canonica == t, ]; FI <- lee(t, "0_Ficha"); MU <- lee(t, "1_Muestra"); ES <- lee(t, "3_Fiabilidad_estabilidad")
  VE <- lee(t, "4b_Validez_frente_etiqueta"); BC <- lee(t, "4c_Baja_comprension_posterior")
  data.frame(dom = ct$dominio, Task = sprintf("[%s](%s.en.qmd)", ct$name_en, t), Family = FAM[[ct$familia]], Class = ct$clase, Ages = ct$edades,
             N = if (nrow(MU)) sum(MU$N) else NA, `Stability ρ` = if (nrow(ES)) median(ES$rho) else NA, `α (2021)` = ct$alfa_2021,
             `AUC: persistent difficulty` = mx(VE$AUC), `AUC: later comprehension` = mx(BC$AUC),
             circ = isTRUE(as.logical(FI$circular_con_etiqueta)), check.names = FALSE)
}))
R$`AUC: persistent difficulty` <- ifelse(is.na(R$`AUC: persistent difficulty`), "—", paste0(sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.2f", R$`AUC: persistent difficulty`)), ifelse(R$circ, "*", "")))
R <- R[order(match(R$dom, names(DOM)), R$Class, R$Family, R$Task), ]
```

The task sheets in this part of the English edition cover the `r nrow(R)` assessment tasks of the catalog: `r sum(R$Class == "A")` of class A, with enough reliability and sample size for norms, and `r sum(R$Class != "A")` of classes B and C, which are described but should not be used for individual decisions ([rules](../../limites.en.qmd#sec-clases)). They are generated automatically with the same script as the Spanish ones, so the figures are identical. Each one includes the shared theoretical framework of its construct, the sample, descriptive statistics, reliability, validity, provisional norms, the variables that affect scores and a paragraph for publications.

The hand-written **pilot task sheets** go further than the automatic ones (theoretical framework, rigor analyses, studies they open up): [Reading speed in words per minute](../VEL.en.qmd), [Letter knowledge](../LET.en.qmd), [TECLE](../TECLE.en.qmd), [Syllable counting](../CF523.en.qmd) and [Rapid automatized naming](../RAN.en.qmd).

```{r}
#| output: asis
for (d in intersect(names(DOM), unique(R$dom))) {
  cat("\n\n## ", DOM[[d]], "\n\n", sep = "")
  T <- R[R$dom == d, setdiff(names(R), c("dom", "circ"))]; rownames(T) <- NULL
  print(tabla(T, digitos = 2))
}
```

\* Circular: the persistent difficulty label is built with this task, so the AUC shows agreement, not prediction.
